slides.title: Out of breath by lap two?
slides.sub: It is often your technique, not your fitness

slides.title: Breathe into your ribs
slides.body: Folded low, your belly is blocked by your thighs. Breathe into the sides and back of your ribcage instead. Do not sit up to breathe, it costs you speed.

slides.title: Never hold your breath
slides.body: Many skaters hold a big breath through the start and the first corner. Keep your trunk braced but let the air move, with a steady controlled exhale.

slides.title: Time your breathing to the lap
slides.caption: Exhale steadily through each corner and take one full inhale on each straight.

slides.title: Ease into cold rink air
slides.body: Build intensity gradually so your first hard effort is not your first effort. Nose breathe in the easy warm up and sip water through the session.

slides.title: Check the kit that squeezes
slides.body: A neck guard pressing on the windpipe or an undersuit a size too small takes part of every breath. Adjust the fit, and never race without a neck guard.

slides.text: Two full breaths beat five panicked half breaths.
